My girlfriend Maric tells me what I need from life will come in some form or another. I’m leaning my head against the smudged fingerprints of a payphone at a Shell Station my tie loosened and the top buttons of my blue Oxford undone, free from an interview at the Creative Testament Marketing Firm. Marie says the subconscious works like an autopilot, constantly navigating the soul. It’s intuition, what Jung calls our sixth sense, she says. There’s a quaver to her voice like she really believes these things. She clicks over toa call on the other line. I wait, wondering whether she’s trying to cheer me up or test her comprehension of some book she’s been reading. Two children with chocolate smeared smiles peek at me from the back of the van. A man wearing a fishing hat fails to stop the gas pump on $20 and thumps the roof of his Suburban. Marie never comes back to me.

After a couple months of disheartening interviews and dismal projections in the classified ads, I’m apt to bide my time and wait for this subconscious to take over. So I’m back stocking groceries at Kroger, my fallback job.
